note: Machine-readable index of reverse-engineering findings. Scrape this file rather than the prose. 'status' is the field that matters: verified findings were tested, retracted ones were WRONG and are kept so nobody re-derives them.

status_values.verified: tested against game data with a stated method; safe to build on
status_values.probable: consistent with the data but not independently confirmed
status_values.retracted: previously claimed here and since DISPROVED - do not use

findings.title: Per-effect FX parameters live in EmitterGraphParams (RFL2 field hash 0x4832AD52)
findings.summary: 60/60 sampled fx EBX carry it, 4-60 entries each. Name resolved via the reference's sdk_field_names.tsv. Our earlier 'second unnamed GpuExposedParameterInput table (f_512_4832ad52)' and 'an EmitterGraphParams array that is empty' were the SAME field described twice.

findings.title: EmitterGraphParams element layout: float4 value @+0, u32 PropertyId @+32, stride 64
findings.summary: Settled by a uniqueness test, not by eyeballing bytes. Stride 48 looks plausible from raw bytes but decodes ids as floats-read-as-ints (0x3F800000 = 1.0f). Test that a candidate id slot is non-zero AND distinct across elements.

findings.title: FX PropertyIds are GPU-exposed parameter ids, NOT RFL2 field hashes
findings.summary: Different namespace - the reference's field-name tables cannot resolve them (Color0/Color1 are absent from all of them). 68 names recovered by dictionary lookup with a control run: 68 real named vs 0 fake named.

findings.title: An fx_* effect is N LAYERS; each layer references an eg_* emitter template
findings.summary: eg_* values are DEFAULTS - eg_gs_basicsmoke_01 and eg_gs_basicfire_01 have IDENTICAL named parameters; the sprite is what differs. 247 of 288 sampled fx_* are multi-layer (up to 10). Merging instances destroys the authored variation - read parameters per instance.

findings.title: 79% of FX tint parameters are near-grey - effect colour comes from the TEXTURE
findings.summary: 4,921 of 6,218 color0/color1/randomcolormin/randomcolormax values across 471 effects have saturation < 0.10. For each effect's visually dominant layer it is 85% at saturation < 0.02 (pure white). Tint-driven colour previews therefore cannot match the game; the emitter's texture is the real source.

findings.title: In-game FX video failed a shuffled-pairing control as a colour oracle
findings.summary: Measured vs manifest hue gave a median error of 15.3 deg, which looks excellent - but shuffling the pairing scored 15.2 deg and 338/400 random pairings BEAT the true one. After excluding sky, 98% of measured hues fall in a 10-50 deg band, so the measurement is a constant; correlation with manifest hue is 0.020. Always run the shuffled control before believing an FX colour-agreement number.

findings.title: Three loop-invariant rebuilds cost 12.6x - MeshSet lookup was a full tree walk per mesh
findings.summary: find_meshset() ran a recursive glob over the whole bundles tree per mesh per prop, measured at ~6s per lookup. Also: MVDB variation resolve rebuilt two guid-index-wide tables per file (2.03s x 17,079 = 9.6h), and every worker re-globbed the same 23,053 blueprints. Assembly went 27.2 -> 342.4 props/min, CPU 30% -> 92%. Diagnose with py-spy dump --pid <pid> --nonblocking.

findings.title: Reading burned-in text from frames without an OCR engine
findings.summary: Threshold the band, fit the type's pitch lattice to reject sparks, then SCORE every known candidate name against the glyph bitmaps instead of decoding to text (free decoding confuses F/E, p/c, n/m, w/v at low res). Output can only ever be a name that exists in the game data. 241/533 segments resolved to 122 effects, 238/240 adjacent pairs in correct alphabetical order.
